_readme: Single source for the en/ site root (nav, SEO, catalog, sitemap). Human-readable fields are translation units tracked in i18n/ledger.json. Rebuild with: SITE_ROOT=en node scripts/build_nav.js

site.title: Woow n8n Onboarding Guide
site.subtitle: Hand your repetitive work over to automation
site.description: A Traditional Chinese n8n tutorial with 22 chapters and 3 appendices: from signing in, using someone else’s template, and building your first workflow through expressions, the Code node, AI Agent, and Webhook—so your company can hand repetitive work over to automation.
site.footerMeta: Screenshots are taken from the official Home Assistant interface. Home Assistant is a trademark of the Open Home Foundation. This site is not affiliated with it.

hub._readme: index.html is the four-category Resource Hub, maintained by hand and not changed by build_nav. build_nav generates the tutorial catalog at the file named by catalog. pages lists the standalone single-file handbooks under the hub; each has its own head and styles and is included in the sitemap and check_links allowlist.

chapters.title: What n8n is, and how it differs from Zapier/Make
chapters.card: Why the company chose n8n, how it differs from Zapier/Make, and which repetitive work it can take off your hands.
chapters.description: What n8n is, how it differs from Zapier/Make/Power Automate, why WoowTech chose it, and where it does and does not fit.

chapters.title: Open Woow n8n: sign in and a 5-minute tour
chapters.card: Open n8n.woowtech.io, get your account, confirm that your device can connect, and learn the main parts of the interface.
chapters.description: Sign in to Woow n8n (n8n.woowtech.io), confirm your access, and learn where to find the home page and sidebar.

chapters.title: What the workspace looks like
chapters.card: Learn the canvas, nodes panel, Executions, Templates, and Credentials in one pass so you do not get lost.
chapters.description: A complete tour of the n8n workspace: the canvas, nodes panel, execution history, Templates, and where to find Credentials.

chapters.title: Start from the Templates gallery
chapters.card: n8n already has thousands of ready-made workflows. Copying someone else’s work is the fastest way to start.
chapters.description: A tour of the n8n Templates gallery: how to find templates, review ratings and nodes, and copy one into your workspace to run it.

chapters.title: Find JSON on n8n.io and paste it in
chapters.card: n8n.io/workflows has a huge library of shared workflows. Copy and paste the JSON to make one yours.
chapters.description: Import workflow JSON from n8n.io/workflows or a colleague into Woow n8n, with common errors and fixes.

chapters.title: Change someone else's workflow: remap fields, swap the trigger, run it
chapters.card: Using someone else's workflow unchanged is wishful thinking. Learn how to adapt it to your needs.
chapters.description: Edit an existing n8n workflow: change node fields, the trigger and credentials, then select Execute Workflow to run it manually.

chapters.title: The four node families: Trigger / Core / App / Cluster
chapters.card: The nodes panel has hundreds of nodes, but they fall into four families: start, act, control, and AI clusters.
chapters.description: The four families in the n8n nodes panel: Trigger, Core, App (actions/integrations), and Cluster (AI group nodes), with what each means and where to find it.

chapters.title: Your first workflow: push Google Calendar to Slack at 8:00 every morning
chapters.card: Build a useful workflow from scratch: send today’s calendar to Slack at 8:00 every morning.
chapters.description: Build your first n8n workflow step by step: Schedule Trigger + Google Calendar events + Slack message, then run it successfully.

chapters.title: What an item is, and how data moves between nodes
chapters.card: Understand n8n items: how many items a node receives and what the next node gets.
chapters.description: The n8n item data model: JSON structure, each node’s items array, $json / $binary, and how to visualize data flow.

chapters.title: Three triggers: Manual / Schedule / Event
chapters.card: When does a workflow run? Choose manual, scheduled, or external-event triggers.
chapters.description: The three main n8n trigger families: Manual (testing), Schedule (cron), and Event (webhook or SaaS event), with suitable uses and settings.

chapters.title: Popular SaaS integrations: Slack, Gmail, Google Sheets and Drive
chapters.card: Four services office workers connect most often: Slack notifications, Gmail messages, Google Sheets records, and Drive storage.
chapters.description: A quick reference for common n8n SaaS nodes: Slack messages, Gmail mail, Google Sheets reads and writes, Google Drive uploads, and key OAuth settings.

chapters.title: The HTTP Request node: reach every API without an official integration
chapters.card: Use the HTTP Request node for services without a ready-made n8n node. It handles 80% of custom integrations.
chapters.description: A complete guide to the n8n HTTP Request node: GET/POST/PUT/DELETE, headers, body, authentication, pagination, and common error handling.

chapters.title: Managing credentials: keys, OAuth, and where sharing stops
chapters.card: A workflow needs access to your accounts to work for you. Learn how to store and share that access safely.
chapters.description: The n8n Credentials system: create, edit and delete credentials; OAuth authorization; team sharing; shared-account risks; and secret storage.

chapters.title: Expressions: it all starts with {{ $json.field }}
chapters.card: Use an expression when a node field needs data from an earlier node. This chapter covers the five forms you will use most.
chapters.description: An introduction to n8n expressions: {{ $json.field }} for the current item, $node['name'] for a named node, date functions, string concatenation, and common errors.

chapters.title: IF / Switch: conditional branching
chapters.card: Send values over 100 down branch A and values under 100 down branch B: build conditions visually.
chapters.description: Conditional branching in n8n: IF for two branches, Switch for many, comparison operators, combined conditions, and different downstream paths.

chapters.title: Merge / Loop Over Items / Split Out / Aggregate: working with many items
chapters.card: Process many items, combine several paths, and split arrays—the data plumbing in n8n.
chapters.description: n8n nodes for multiple items: Merge, Loop Over Items (formerly Split In Batches), Split Out, and Aggregate, with a Google Sheets row-notification example.

chapters.title: Error handling: error workflow / retry / wait
chapters.card: What happens when a workflow fails overnight? Add an error workflow, retries, and waits.
chapters.description: Three n8n error-handling techniques: catch failures in an error workflow, retry individual nodes, and use Wait to avoid rate limits, including scheduled-failure notifications.

chapters.title: Set / Edit Fields: shape data without writing code
chapters.card: Add fields to JSON, rename them, and rearrange them without writing code.
chapters.description: A complete guide to the n8n Set node (called Edit Fields since v1): add, rename, reorder, and flatten fields, including shaping an API payload into one sheet row.

chapters.title: Sub-workflow: pull shared logic into its own workflow
chapters.card: Using the same logic in five workflows? Extract a sub-workflow and update it once for all callers.
chapters.description: The n8n sub-workflow pattern: call it with Execute Workflow, pass parameters, receive return values, and extract reusable utilities such as shared Slack notifications.

chapters.title: Code node: a few lines of JavaScript inside a workflow
chapters.card: When ready-made nodes cannot shape the data, the Code node is your escape hatch. Beginners can start by copying the examples.
chapters.description: An introduction to the n8n Code node: JavaScript / Python modes, $input.all() / return formats, and four common patterns—filter, map, aggregate, and split.

chapters.title: AI Agent: give a workflow a node that thinks
chapters.card: Ordinary nodes follow rules. AI Agent can make judgments for customer support and data organization.
chapters.description: The n8n AI Agent node family (LangChain): combine Chat Trigger + AI Agent + Chat Model + Memory, add tools, and apply common customer-support and data-organization patterns.

chapters.title: Webhook: let outside systems call into n8n
chapters.card: Forms, HA triggers, and LINE messages all enter n8n through the Webhook node.
chapters.description: A complete guide to the n8n Webhook node: Test URL vs Production URL, HTTP methods, authentication, response modes, and LINE bot / form / HA automation examples.

appendices.title: Settings reference
appendices.card: Execution retention, timezone, log level, and what Personal and Workspace settings control.
appendices.description: n8n Settings reference: execution retention, timezone, log level, and the difference between user and Workspace settings.

appendices.title: Error troubleshooting
appendices.card: Red nodes, timeouts, expired credentials, 429 rate limits, and missing sub-workflows—symptoms matched to fixes.
appendices.description: A symptom-based guide to common n8n errors: red node borders, timeouts, expired credentials, 429 rate limits, missing webhooks, and sub-workflow failures, with 2–3 fixes for each.

appendices.title: How it works underneath, for the curious
appendices.card: Community vs Cloud vs Enterprise, self-hosting choices, queue mode, and databases.
appendices.description: A deeper look at n8n architecture: Community / Cloud / Enterprise differences, self-hosted deployment, queue mode, SQLite vs Postgres, and backup strategy.
